newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber extends losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber extends losses at close.

text.p: Rubber prices continued to fall at the close as sentiment remained bearish due to buyers' unwillingness to commit themselves, dealers said.
"Sentiment is still bearish. Buyers are staying away while waiting for cheaper levels," a dealer at a trading firm said.
Weakness in the Tokyo market also discouraged buyers, dealers said. "The buyers know that prices can get cheaper if they wait," one said.
Inquiries from South Korea and scattered Chinese interest for SMR 10 grades and latex prices were seen, dealers said.
Dealers offered SMR CV at 315 cents, SMR L at 295, SMR 10 at 248, SMR 20 at 246 and latex at 215-216.
Demand for latex also dwindled considerably and the market does not expect much inquiries from Europe because of the summer holidays.
"We are also concerned about the baht and what the Thai government will do. This may affect bank lending to the local rubber industry," another trader said.
At the close, July RSS1 buyer eased 1.50 cents to 267.50 cents ($1.06) a kg and July SMR 20 buyer was down 2.50 cents at 246.50 cents.
